title: Micro-Repair
concept: The smallest way to make up, for when something small has stung: one of you softens your tone and owns the impact in a sentence, before it hardens into something bigger. We’d take a clumsy repair today over a perfect one next week.
whenToUse: When your tone’s getting sharp, something small stung, or a full repair feels like too much right now but waiting will only make it worse. Timing: start within minutes if you can; complete within 24 hours.
steps: Do one small thing — an action, or own your part out loud.
Sit side by side instead of face to face if that’s easier.
Say you noticed the impact — one sentence, no “but”.
Take one tiny next step — or take a Pause + Return.

phrases.text: That came out sharp. Let me try again.
One small thing: I can own ___.
I saw that hurt you. I’m sorry for ___.

working: A snaps about the bins. Thirty seconds later: “That came out sharp.” They sit on the sofa, side by side, and A owns the tone. By bedtime they’re talking about tomorrow.
notWorking: You wait for “the real talk this weekend” while every evening in between stays tense. Skip enough small repairs and the tension builds.
activity: Pick one small unfinished thing from today. Soften your tone, own your part, and make one small ask. Start within minutes if you can; complete within 24 hours.
